prompt.context: Your client is a beverage company. 5 years ago, the company earned $1 billion in sales. However, in the last 5 years, sales have fallen to $800 million. Profits have also fallen from $150 million to $100 million in the last 5 years. You have been hired to determine why this company is seeing a decline and to determine what they could do differently.
prompt.question: Why is the company seeing a decline in sales and profits, and what could they do differently?

clarifying_info.q: What products does the company make?
clarifying_info.a: The company makes 2 products: Fruit Juice (100% juice, healthy) and Fruit Drink (has sugar, chemicals, water; accounts for 95% of sales).

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall market size and who are the competitors?
clarifying_info.a: The overall size of the market is $1.5 billion. There are 2 other main competitors: Player B with market share of $400 million, and Player C with market share of $300 million.
Player B produces Fruit Juice and revenues have increased in the last 5 years. Player C produces Fruit Juice and Fruit Drink, and revenues have been flat over the last 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: What are the profit margins on each product?
clarifying_info.a: Profit margins on Fruit Drink are $0.25/case. Profit margins on Fruit Juice are $0.15/case.

framework: Company: Distribution channels, Products and pricing, Revenues and costs, Marketing and advertising
Market: Growing/flat/declining overall market, Competitor products and pricing
Customers: Brand perception, Demographics, Changing consumer trends toward healthier lifestyles

questions.prompt: What do you think has caused the declining sales and profits for the company?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that changing consumer trends toward healthier lifestyles has driven growth in Fruit Juice while the client’s 95% revenue concentration in Fruit Drink (less healthy) is the root cause of sales decline. Costs have also increased because producing 100% fruit juice is more expensive than a diluted drink with chemicals, water, and sugar, explaining the profit decline. Candidate should suggest the company reposition itself to focus on Fruit Juice products.

questions.prompt: Consumers like the client’s brand and associate it with high-quality products. However, consumers question the client’s credibility in the healthier Fruit Juice segment, and Player B’s marketing has been attacking the client’s credibility. What should the client do?
questions.guidance: This is a brainstorming question. A strong candidate generates multiple actionable ideas across marketing, product, and distribution dimensions.

questions.prompt: Profit margins on Fruit Drink are $0.25/case and on Fruit Juice are $0.15/case. What should the client think about when determining how much production it should transfer from Fruit Drink to Fruit Juice?
questions.guidance: The client must build a business case for the shift given that Fruit Drink margins are $0.10/case higher than Fruit Juice. Key considerations: (1) conduct detailed market research to determine whether the trend toward healthier lifestyles will continue; (2) consider raising Fruit Juice prices to close the margin gap; (3) find ways to reduce Fruit Juice production costs. The decision depends on long-run market trajectory, not just current margins.

math.setup: Margin difference per case: $0.25 - $0.15 = $0.10 in favor of Fruit Drink
math.answer: Fruit Drink currently earns $0.10/case more than Fruit Juice, so any production transfer sacrifices margin unless prices rise or costs fall.

questions.prompt: The client is owned by a PE firm looking to sell the company in the next 3 years. What would you tell the PE firm regarding changing the management team?
questions.guidance: This depends on the PE firm’s portfolio. If the PE firm owns other complementary companies with experienced management teams in the beverage space, it should consider using that outside management team—especially if that team has a track record of quick turnarounds in this business area.

questions.prompt: The client is instead owned by an agricultural co-op of 900 farmers. A big beverage company (e.g., Pepsi) has offered to purchase the client at a significant premium. The co-op is hesitant to sell. Why might that be?
questions.guidance: Two main reasons: (1) A company like Pepsi has established supply sources and may stop sourcing from the agricultural co-op, causing the farmers to lose profits and jobs. (2) A cultural issue: the agricultural co-op does not want to ‘sell out’ to corporate America.

brainstorming.prompt: Consumers like the client’s brand and associate it with high-quality products. However, consumers question the client’s credibility in the healthier Fruit Juice segment. Player B’s marketing has especially been attacking the client’s credibility. What should the client do?

categories.name: Product & Labeling
ideas: Re-label products to emphasize 100% fruit juice, not from concentrate

categories.name: Marketing & Advertising
ideas: Highlight health association in marketing campaigns and advertising
Market to parents, since children are less focused on healthy attributes

categories.name: Distribution & Partnerships
ideas: Partner with fitness centers to distribute trials and promotional materials

recommendation: The client should reposition its product portfolio away from Fruit Drink and toward Fruit Juice to align with the consumer trend toward healthier lifestyles
In the near term, invest in re-labeling and marketing campaigns that assert credibility in the healthy Fruit Juice segment
risks: Fruit Juice margins ($0.15/case) are currently $0.10/case lower than Fruit Drink ($0.25/case), so a rapid shift without price increases or cost reductions will compress overall profitability
The health trend may plateau or reverse, leaving the company over-invested in a lower-margin product
next_steps: Conduct detailed market research to assess durability of the health and wellness trend
Explore pricing power for Fruit Juice and identify cost-reduction opportunities in production
Develop a phased production transfer plan with clear margin and volume milestones
